_comment: These are hard numeric limits. Claude's reasoning/thesis step may NEVER override these values. Any proposed trade that violates a rule here must be rejected before it reaches review_equity_order, with no exceptions regardless of how strong the thesis sounds.
account_number_note: Intentionally not stored in this repo. The scheduled run prompt supplies the trading account number at runtime; use that value wherever a spec says account_number.

execution.note: mode must be manually changed from 'dry_run' to 'live' by the human. Claude must never change this value itself, and must refuse to place live orders while mode is 'dry_run'.

universe.supplementary_scan_note: Robinhood scan -- define whatever screening conditions you like (relative volume, market cap, RSI, etc.) via the Robinhood MCP's create_scan tool, then paste its scan_id here. Additive to watchlist_max_candidates, not shared with it -- the watchlist's own slots are never crowded out by scan results.
universe.max_market_cap_note: Effectively no upper limit (USD 100T) so the largest companies qualify.

signal_thresholds._comment: A Step-1 candidate qualifies for a Research-run news search + thesis (i.e. counts as a 'notable signal') if it meets ANY ONE of these three, computed from data already pulled in Steps 1-2 (no extra API calls). This is a mechanical gate, not a judgment call. Currently-held positions are exempt and always get a thesis regardless of these thresholds.

position_sizing.v2_note: Strategy v2. risk_per_trade_pct caps each new entry so that its loss at the initial stop is about this share of the account: size = min(conviction_pct for its tier, risk_per_trade_pct / stop distance), then the usual multipliers. It can only make a position smaller than its conviction tier, never larger. max_positions_per_sector blocks a new tactical entry that would put more than this many tactical positions in one sector (sectors merged through concentration_report.sector_groups, ETFs through etf_sectors); the core sleeve never counts. Both are applied by scripts/position_sizing.py.
position_sizing.note: Sized for an account of roughly $500 to $1,500: up to 8 tactical positions, high 12%, medium 8%, low 5% of the account, so single-stock risk stays moderate and cash is left for second tranches. For a small account (under about $500), 6 positions at 15/10/7.5% keeps each position large enough to matter. A new position smaller than min_new_position_usd (after pullback, loss-limit, or regime multipliers) is skipped rather than bought as dust. The core sleeve (SPY/QQQ) is separate and does not count toward max_concurrent_positions. Positions bought under earlier, larger sizes are never force-sold to the new size; conviction_trim trims one that stays overweight once its conviction is no longer high. Revisit when the account passes about $1,500 (e.g. 10 positions at 10/7/4%).
position_sizing.min_top_up_note: A top-up only fires if the computed buy amount clears max($1.00 broker minimum, min_top_up_usd, min_top_up_pct_of_target x target_size for that candidate's conviction tier). Below that, skip without calling review_equity_order -- a top-up smaller than this doesn't move the position meaningfully, and letting headroom shrink toward zero every cycle otherwise generates a long tail of dust-sized orders as the position converges on target. Applies to top-ups only, never to new-entry sizing.

stop_loss.mode_note: mode is conviction_tiered_atr (the tiers below) or fixed_pct (a flat fixed_pct below the reference price for every tactical position; the tiers are then unused). Either way the ratchet, the trailing stop, the close-based trigger, and hard_floor_pct apply, and an earnings-engine position starts from its engine stop.
stop_loss.v2_note: Strategy v2. Stops trigger on the daily close, not on an intraday print: the Trade run and the hourly check compare the latest official close with the stop, and the closing check uses the price a few minutes before the close as that close. During the day a position is sold only on an emergency (the price below the stop and down at least intraday_emergency_drop_pct from yesterday's close) or at the hard floor, which is always checked against the live price. trailing is a chandelier stop: once the highest close since entry is at least activate_after_gain_atr x ATR(14) above the average cost, the stop rises to that highest close minus atr_multiplier x ATR(14) whenever that is higher; like every stop it only ratchets up. When mode is fixed_pct, the trailing stop instead takes over once the highest close is activate_after_gain_pct_fixed_mode above the average cost, so a small early gain never pulls a wide fixed stop up close to the price. An earnings-engine position starts from its engine stop (just under the gap day's low) instead of the tiered ATR stop.
stop_loss.note: Computed by scripts/stop_loss.py. The tier is the conviction AT ENTRY (recorded in the paper ledger) and never changes; the stop is tier multiplier x ATR(14), clamped to the tier's range, placed just under support when that fits the range; it only ratchets up, never down; and no position may lose more than hard_floor_pct from its average cost. Every open position is checked every run, independent of any new thesis. A good new narrative never cancels a stop-loss.

take_profit.note: Tiered partial take-profit, not a single full-exit threshold. Every open position must have this checked on every cycle, independent of any new thesis about the stock — this account is short-term oriented, not buy-and-hold. A good new narrative does not cancel a take-profit tier any more than it cancels a stop-loss. Each tier fires once (per holding period, i.e. since the position last closed to zero) when gain first reaches it -- a tier whose sell was declined, expired, or skipped fires again on the next run -- selling sell_fraction_of_position of the position's quantity at that moment — see TRADE_TASK.md Step 5 for the exact mechanics. After all three tiers have fired, the remaining quantity is held long indefinitely; only the stop-loss still applies to it. See sell_reentry_lock for re-entry lock behavior.

conviction_trim.note: Trims a held position to its conviction-tier target once conviction has been 'low' or 'medium' (i.e. not 'high') for min_overweight_conviction_cycles consecutive cycles and the overage exceeds overweight_trigger_pct -- see scripts/conviction_trim.py. See sell_reentry_lock for re-entry lock behavior.

sell_reentry_lock.note: Applies to every sell reason: a loss-closed sell locks re-entry until price drops below the sale price; a gain-closed sell locks until price drops below the sale price or gain_close_max_trading_days trading days pass, whichever comes first. See scripts/entry_gate.py.

loss_limits.note: A normal breach does not pause buying: new positions and top-ups are sized at soft_breach_size_multiplier for soft_breach_trading_days trading days (counting the breach day). Only a severe breach pauses new entries, top-ups, and core buys for that day. Loss limits never force a sell.

regime.basis: SPY daily close vs SPY 200-day average

core_sleeve.note: Strategy v2 (scripts/core_regime.py): the sleeve is on while SPY is above its 200-day average and turns off only after regime.confirm_closes daily closes in a row below it, and back on only after as many closes in a row above it; in between the previous state holds, so one close across the line never flips it (the v1 50-day rule flipped four times in nine days). The ETF is QQQ while QQQ has closed above its own 200-day average regime.confirm_closes times in a row, otherwise SPY; a held core ETF is rotated only on the same confirmation. Holds target_pct_of_account and rebalances only when the core value drifts more than rebalance_band_pct of total value from target. SPY and QQQ are traded ONLY through the core sleeve, never as tactical positions. A core position exits when the regime turns off, or at the hard floor.

entry_engines.note: Strategy v2 (scripts/setups.py). New tactical positions come only from an entry engine, the pullback whitelist (pullback_mode), or the defensive slot; buying a stock just because it is trending up (v1 trend entries) is off. dip: a stock still above its 200-day average that has closed down min_down_days days in a row or has RSI(2) at or below max_rsi2 (a one-day drop larger than max_single_day_drop_pct is news, not a dip, and is skipped); it is sold on the first close above its exit_close_above_sma-day average, after max_hold_trading_days sessions, or at its stop. earnings: post-earnings drift after a report with an EPS beat and raised guidance, where the stock opened at least min_gap_pct above the prior close on at least min_rel_volume x its 20-day average volume and held the gap into the close (still min_gap_pct up, upper half of the day's range); it may be bought within entry_window_trading_days sessions after the gap day, its stop sits stop_buffer_below_gap_low_pct under the gap day's low, and it is sold after max_hold_trading_days sessions or at the stop. Engine exits are reasons engine_exit and time_stop. requires_above_sma200, require_eps_beat, require_guidance_raised, and trend_entries_enabled document fixed parts of v2 (scripts/setups.py and the specs always apply them); changing them has no effect. top_ups: held positions are added to only as a pullback second tranche. Positions opened before v2 keep their mode and are managed by the stops (now close-based with the trailing stop) and take-profit.

pullback_mode.note: Whitelisted names may be bought below their 200-day average when at least min_pct_below_52wk_high below the 52-week high, scripts/technicals.py reports stabilizing=true (at least 2 of 4 stabilization signals and no falling-knife flag), and there is no thesis-breaking company news. Entry is staged: half size first, the other half as a top-up once the rebound is confirmed within the window. The entry_extension gate does not apply to pullback entries; entry_price_gap and earnings_blackout still do.

defensive.note: In a small growth account, defensive names are a parking place, not a core holding: at most one defensive position, and only bought while the broad market is risk-off. Existing defensive positions are still managed normally when the regime turns.

regime_sizing.note: While SPY is below its 200-day average, new tactical entries and top-ups are sized at new_entry_size_multiplier (multiplied with any pullback or loss-limit multiplier). It does not apply to the core sleeve (which already exits below the 200-day average) or to the defensive slot, and never forces a sell.

performance_guard.note: Tighten-only feedback from the weekly review. Each Sunday, scripts/performance_review.py looks at positions fully closed in the last lookback_calendar_days (one per holding period, however many lots or partial sales it had); any buy type (trend, pullback, etf, defensive) or entry-conviction tier with at least min_closed_positions closed positions whose win rate is below max_win_rate AND whose average return is below max_avg_return_pct is written to performance_guard.json. The Trade run, the manual check, and the hourly and closing checks' buy retries then size new entries and top-ups in a guarded buy type or tier at size_multiplier (applied once, even if both match), multiplied with any other multiplier. It lifts automatically when a later review no longer finds the bucket failing. It can only reduce size (size_multiplier must be between 0 and 1), never forces a sell, never touches the core sleeve, and ignores a performance_guard.json older than max_age_days.

concentration_report.note: The report is information only: the separate cap position_sizing.max_positions_per_sector counts positions per sector with the same merging. every Trade and manual run reports each sector's share of the account (scripts/concentration.py) and flags any sector above flag_sector_pct at the top of the report. sector_groups merges Robinhood's fine-grained sector names; etf_sectors labels ETFs, so the core sleeve counts toward the sector it is concentrated in.

earnings_hold.note: For positions already held (new buys are covered by earnings_blackout): every Trade and manual run flags held positions whose next earnings report is within flag_window_trading_days, and on the last regular session before the report sells trim_fraction_of_position of positions whose entry conviction is in trim_convictions, once per report (scripts/earnings_risk.py). Core-sleeve positions are skipped. The trim goes through the normal sell procedure and app approval.

etf_tactical.note: ETFs other than the core sleeve (currently SMH) are ranked by the Research run's etf_conviction (ETF rubric in RESEARCH_TASK.md), not the company-catalyst conviction.

wash_sale_avoidance.note: Toggle only -- set enabled to false to turn this guard off entirely; no other change needed. IRS wash-sale rule applies per taxpayer across ALL accounts, not per account, so this checks linked_accounts, not just account_number. Blocks BUYS only (new entries and top-ups) -- never blocks a stop_loss/take_profit/exit_existing sell, since risk management must never bend to a tax outcome; those sells are instead logged with a wash-sale flag if one applies, for the human's own tax tracking. This cannot prevent a wash sale caused by a purchase made LATER in another linked account after an agentic-account sell -- those accounts are outside this pipeline's control; only the human can avoid that side.
wash_sale_avoidance.linked_accounts_note: Intentionally not stored in this repo; the run prompt supplies it. The MCP account is treated as a standalone account: linked_accounts contains only the trading account itself, so holdings and activity in any other account are never read or considered.

stop_alerts.note: Keeps one Robinhood price_below alert at each held position's stop price (see TRADE_TASK.md Step 5 and HOURLY_TASK.md), so a sharp intraday drop notifies the human in real time instead of waiting for the next run. Real positions always get alerts; set include_paper_positions to true to also get alerts for dry-run paper positions. The agent only ever touches alert IDs it recorded in agent_alerts.json, and never deletes alerts.

entry_price_gap.note: Hard ceiling on buys -- a gap this large skips the buy this cycle even if the thesis still reads fine, same principle as a stop-loss. Never applies to sells. Checked in the Trade run's Step 4 (price-based staleness check), before Step 5's risk enforcement -- not part of the execution.mode live-order gate.

entry_extension.note: Hard ceiling on buys -- skips the buy this cycle if current_price is more than max_extension_pct above its own lookback_trading_days-day moving average, same principle as entry_price_gap. Never applies to sells.

earnings_blackout.note: Skips new entries and top-ups when the symbol's next earnings report is within blackout_trading_days trading days (0 = today), so fresh money isn't put on a binary event. Never applies to sells.

early_exit_guard.note: Within window_trading_days of a holding period's opening buy, an exit_existing sell requires a new_fact_date after the entry thesis's date -- a thesis can't reverse on facts it already had. Never blocks stop_loss/take_profit/conviction_trim.

intraday_checks.note: Used by the hourly and closing checks (HOURLY_TASK.md). A held position down news_trigger_drop_from_prev_close_pct from yesterday's close, or moved news_trigger_move_since_last_check_pct either way since the previous check, gets one news search; if company news breaks the thesis and news_exit_enabled is true, the whole position is submitted for sale (reason news_exit), always for the account owner's approval. A drop of market_drop_alert_pct in SPY or QQQ only adds a warning to the report. With resubmit_declined_sells, a declined stop-loss, take-profit, or news-exit sell, and in the closing check a declined dip engine exit, is submitted again at the next check while its rule still fires. buy_retry lets the checks retry today's candidates the morning run skipped only for price (entry_price_gap, entry_extension), slots, cash, or the sector cap (max_positions_per_sector), or whose buy was declined or expired, through every buy gate again, with at most max_filled_buys_per_symbol_per_day filled buys per symbol per day. scripts/intraday_triggers.py applies the price triggers; scripts/log_query.py finds the retry candidates.
